question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
option_1: Yesterday, we will be painting the door when a neighbour stops by to say hello.
option_2: Yesterday, we are painting the door when a neighbour stop by to say hello.
option_3: Yesterday, we was painting the door when a neighbour stopping by to say hello.
option_4: Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "Yesterday" fixes the action firmly in the past, so the whole sentence must be in the past tense.

• A longer background action interrupted by a shorter one uses past continuous (was/were + -ing) for the longer action and simple past (V2) for the interrupting action: "we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by".

◦ Correct: Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses the future "will be painting" with "Yesterday".

• Option 2 uses the present "are painting / stop"; Option 3 uses the wrong plural form "we was" and the non-finite "stopping".

NOTE

• Structure: When + past simple interrupts an ongoing past continuous action — "While I was reading, the phone rang."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The coaches decided to _____ the regulations more strictly because the candidates were not paying attention during their training sessions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. enforce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enforce" means to make sure that a rule or law is obeyed; to impose compliance. Rules/regulations are things one "enforces". (लागू करना / पालन कराना)

◦ Correct: The coaches decided to enforce the regulations more strictly ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "enjoy", Option 2 "provide" and Option 4 "supply" do not collocate with "regulations more strictly" and change the intended meaning.

NOTE

• Common collocations: enforce a law / rule / regulation / discipline / ban. Related word: "reinforce" (to strengthen).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I checked the ____________ to see if it will rain or not.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Weather" (a noun) means the state of the atmosphere — rain, sunshine, temperature, etc. One checks the "weather" to know if it will rain. (मौसम)

◦ Correct: I checked the weather to see if it will rain or not.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• These are homophones: "whether" (a conjunction showing a choice — whether or not), "wither" (a verb — to dry up / shrivel) and "wether" (a castrated ram) do not fit.

NOTE

• Remember the trio: weather (मौसम) vs whether (क्या / चाहे) vs wither (मुरझाना). The blank needs the atmospheric noun "weather".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Although she is virtuous in her deeds, people misinterpret her because of her open and bold nature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wicked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Virtuous" means having high moral standards; righteous and good. Its antonym is "wicked", meaning morally bad or evil. (सदाचारी का विलोम — दुष्ट)

◦ Example: A virtuous person does good; a wicked person does harm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "moral" and Option 4 "commendable" are synonyms of virtuous.

• Option 1 "sane" (of sound mind) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of virtuous: moral, righteous, upright, honourable. Antonyms: wicked, sinful, immoral, corrupt.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Concieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Concieve" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conceive", meaning to form an idea / to become pregnant. (कल्पना करना / गर्भधारण करना)

◦ Correct spelling: CON + CEIVE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Separate", "Accessible" and "Convenience" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Spelling rule: "i before e, except after c" — so it is receive, deceive, conceive, perceive (after 'c' → 'ei').

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner had they left their home that it started raining heavily.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. their home than it started.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "No sooner ... than" is a fixed pair (not "no sooner ... that"). It follows inversion: "No sooner had + subject + V3 than + past simple".

◦ Correct: No sooner had they left their home than it started raining heavily.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly keeps "that" and uses "start"; Option 2 wrongly uses the present "starts"; Option 3 uses the wrong spelling "there" (should be the possessive "their").

NOTE

• Similar correlatives with inversion: "Hardly/Scarcely ... when", "No sooner ... than". Both describe one event happening immediately after another.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

Something that has the quality of being easily broken
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Brittle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brittle" means hard but liable to break easily; fragile. It exactly fits "something that has the quality of being easily broken". (भंगुर / आसानी से टूटने वाला)

◦ Example: Glass and dry twigs are brittle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Broken" describes something already broken, not the quality of breaking easily.

• Option 3 "Damage" is a noun/verb for harm; Option 4 "Hard" is the near opposite here.

NOTE

• Related words: fragile (easily damaged), frail (weak), flimsy (thin and weak). Antonyms of brittle: sturdy, tough, durable.

question:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Sean is notorious for revealing the secrets about the company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Spilling the beans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to spill the beans" means to reveal secret information (usually accidentally or carelessly). It matches "revealing the secrets about the company". (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Example: He spilled the beans about the surprise party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in bad blood" (feeling of hatred), Option 2 "bite the bullet" (to face a difficult situation bravely) and Option 4 "bite the dust" (to fail / die) do not fit.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about revealing secrets: "let the cat out of the bag", "give the game away", "blow the whistle"

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I have a __________ for reading and want to become a writer when I grow up.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. passion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Passion" means a strong, intense enthusiasm or love for something. "A passion for reading" is a natural collocation showing deep interest. (गहरी रुचि / जुनून)

◦ Correct: I have a passion for reading and want to become a writer ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tallow" (animal fat used for candles/soap) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "unity" (oneness) and Option 3 "dream" do not collocate with "a ___ for reading" as naturally ("passion for" is the fixed pattern).

NOTE

• Collocation: "a passion for" (music/reading/art). Related words: zeal, fervour, enthusiasm, ardour.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Solving the riddle given by our teacher is farther beyond our capacity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. far.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Far beyond" is the correct phrase meaning well outside / much more than one's capacity. "Farther" refers to physical/literal distance, which does not suit an abstract "capacity".

◦ Correct: Solving the riddle ... is far beyond our capacity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fair" (just / light-coloured) and Option 2 "fare" (a bus/train charge or food) are homophones that do not fit.

• Option 3 "farthest" is a superlative of distance and is wrong here.

NOTE

• "Farther/farthest" → physical distance; "further/furthest" → extent/degree. With "beyond our capacity" (figurative), we simply use "far beyond"

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I heard management is planning to transfer me to another department and demote me. I need to confirm if this is true by hearing it directly from the person involved and from my manager.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. straight from the horse's mouth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means from the original, most reliable/authoritative source. It matches "hearing it directly from the person involved". (विश्वसनीय स्रोत से सीधे)

◦ Example: I got the news straight from the horse's mouth — the CEO himself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "on pins and needles" (anxious / nervous), Option 3 "in the seventh heaven" (extremely happy) and Option 4 "bearing a grudge" (holding resentment) do not fit.

NOTE

• Related idioms of reliable information: "from a reliable source", "first-hand information"

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

There has been / an increase of the number / of road / accidents recently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. an increase of the number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition is "in", not "of", after "increase" when referring to a rise in quantity: "an increase in the number".

◦ Correct: There has been an increase in the number of road accidents recently.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "There has been", "of road" and "accidents recently" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "an increase in" (a rise in amount/level) — increase in prices, increase in temperature. "Increase of" is used mainly with a figure (an increase of 10%).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the error in the usage of the future tense in the given sentence.

Shivani go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_1: Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_2: Shivani has gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_3: Shivani had gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
option_4: Shivani goes to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "tomorrow" indicates the future, which requires "will + base verb": "Shivani will go".

◦ Correct: Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "has gone" (present perfect) and Option 3 "had gone" (past perfect) are past forms and clash with "tomorrow".

• Option 4 "goes" (simple present) does not express the future intention correctly here.

NOTE

• Simple Future: subject + will/shall + V1 (I will go, She will come). Time markers: tomorrow, next week, soon, later.

question:
Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the underlined word from the options.

He was startled by the loud thander during the storm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thunder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "thunder" — the loud rumbling sound that follows a flash of lightning. (गर्जन / बादल की गरज)

◦ Correct: He was startled by the loud thunder during the storm.

• Spelling key: THUN + DER.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "thondar", "thundar" and "thundre" are all misspellings of "thunder".

NOTE

• Related words: thunderstorm, thunderous (very loud), thunderbolt (a flash of lightning with thunder), lightning (the flash).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Osmium is heavy metal in the periodic table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the heaviest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Comparing one item with all others ("in the periodic table") requires the superlative degree. The superlative of "heavy" is "the heaviest".

◦ Correct: Osmium is the heaviest metal in the periodic table.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more heavy" and Option 4 "the most heavy" are wrong because short adjectives like "heavy" form degrees with "-ier/-iest", not "more/most".

• Option 2 "heavier" (comparative) needs "than" and compares only two things.

NOTE

• Degrees of "heavy": heavy – heavier (than) – the heaviest. Osmium is indeed the densest/heaviest naturally occurring element.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Excessive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Moderate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Excessive" means too much; more than necessary. Its antonym is "moderate", meaning reasonable, limited and not extreme. (अत्यधिक का विलोम — संयमित)

◦ Example: An excessive amount vs a moderate amount.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Inordinate" (unusually large / excessive) is a synonym of excessive.

• Option 2 "Flow" and Option 4 "Desirable" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of excessive: exorbitant, inordinate, immoderate, undue. Antonyms: moderate, reasonable, limited, scanty.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The scientist made an appauling discovery about the environmental impact of the drug.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. appalling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "appalling", meaning shocking, horrifying or extremely bad. (भयावह / अत्यंत बुरा)

◦ Correct: The scientist made an appalling discovery about the environmental impact of the drug.

• Spelling key: AP + PALL + ING (double 'p', double 'l').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "apalling", "appaulling" and "appawling" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related word: "appal/appall" (to horrify). Synonyms of appalling: dreadful, horrific, atrocious, ghastly.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He was constantly / gazing on the / crime scene to / find some clues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gazing on the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "gaze" takes the preposition "at" (or "upon"), not "on". So it should be "gazing at the crime scene".

◦ Correct: He was constantly gazing at the crime scene to find some clues.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "He was constantly", "crime scene to" and "find some clues" are all correct.

NOTE

• Verb + preposition: gaze at, stare at, look at, glance at. We "gaze at" something we look at long and steadily.

question:
Select the most appropriate word from the options to fill in the blank.

Adithya ordered a juicy _________________ cooked to perfection at the highway restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. steak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Steak" is a thick slice of meat (especially beef) for grilling or frying. "A juicy steak cooked to perfection" fits a restaurant context. (मांस का टुकड़ा — स्टेक)

◦ Correct: Adithya ordered a juicy steak cooked to perfection ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "stake" (a wooden post / a bet / a share) and "steak" are homophones; "stink" (a bad smell) and "stoke" (to add fuel to a fire) do not fit.

NOTE

• Homophones: steak (मांस) vs stake (दांव / हिस्सेदारी). "At stake" means at risk.

question:
Select the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence.

The name should also be beneficial to a strong, long-lasting marketing campaign.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Detrimental.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beneficial" means helpful, favourable or advantageous. Its antonym is "detrimental", meaning harmful or damaging. (लाभदायक का विलोम — हानिकारक)

◦ Example: Exercise is beneficial; smoking is detrimental.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Desirable" and Option 3 "Advantageous" are synonyms of beneficial.

• Option 4 "Causal" (relating to a cause) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of beneficial: advantageous, favourable, helpful, valuable. Antonyms: detrimental, harmful, damaging, adverse.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It was just before noon on June 26, 1975, and my friend and I were out exploring the bustling by-lanes of Delhi's Karol Bagh, unaware that the Emergency had been declared, and that it would change our lives in ways we could have never ___1___. Though Indira Gandhi had herself announced the Emergency in a national broadcast at 8 am, IST, the news took its own time to reach the common people who went about their business as always. However, two hours into our outing, we ___2___ something was wrong. The pavement shops began to thin out as we watched and the bigger outlets too looked ready to ___3___; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters. We were young but fancied ourselves as political animals, which at the time was shorthand for being passionately anti-Congress and anti-Indira. There was no way we were going to head home without knowing what had happened. There was already considerable excitement in our small friends' circle over two ___4___ developments: the June 12, 1975 Allahabad high court ruling unseating Indira for electoral malpractices and the Congress's unexpected defeat in the State election in Gujarat. The Supreme Court had allowed Indira to continue as prime minister but that did not ___5___ our joy; it was a technical reprieve that did not lessen the political blow she had received.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. imagined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Imagined" means thought of / pictured in the mind. The Emergency would change their lives "in ways we could have never imagined" — i.e., never anticipated or thought possible. (कल्पना की)

◦ Correct: ... it would change our lives in ways we could have never imagined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "undermined" (weakened), Option 2 "betrothed" (engaged to marry) and Option 3 "targeted" (aimed at) do not fit the sense of "could have never ___".

NOTE

• Collocation: "in ways we could never have imagined" is a common expression conveying something completely unexpected.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. wrap up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "wrap up" means to finish / close down (business for the day). The bigger outlets "looked ready to wrap up", working behind half-downed shutters — i.e., about to shut. (बंद करना / समेटना)

◦ Correct: ... the bigger outlets too looked ready to wrap up; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "open up" is the opposite; Option 2 "pop up" (appear suddenly) and Option 3 "chicken out" (back out from fear) do not fit shops closing.

NOTE

• "Wrap up" also means to summarise/conclude ("let's wrap up the meeting") or to dress warmly ("wrap up well").

◦ Correct: ... excitement ... over two landmark developments: the June 12, 1975 Allahabad high court ruling ... and the Congress's unexpected defeat ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "production" is a noun that does not fit as an adjective here.

• Options 3 "flaws" and 4 "mistakes" carry a negative sense that contradicts the "excitement" the events caused.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dampen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dampen" means to reduce / lessen (a feeling such as enthusiasm or joy). The Supreme Court's technical reprieve "did not dampen our joy" — i.e., did not lessen it. (कम करना / फीका करना)

◦ Correct: ... but that did not dampen our joy; it was a technical reprieve ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "adopted" is grammatically and contextually wrong.

• Option 3 "magnified" (increased) is the opposite; Option 4 "diminished" is close in meaning but the fixed collocation here is "dampen (someone's) joy/spirits/enthusiasm".

NOTE

• Common collocation: "dampen one's spirits / enthusiasm / mood". Synonyms: dishearten, deflate, discourage.
